facts.statement: The name Yuxisaurus kopchicki first appeared in a bioRxiv preprint in late 2021.
facts.quote: The name "Yuxisaurus kopchicki" first appeared in a bioRxiv preprint released in late 2021.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen CVEB 21701 includes a partial skeleton with skull parts, vertebrae, limb bones, and at least 120 osteoderms.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, CVEB 21701, consists of a partial skeleton including parts of the skull, several vertebrae, partial limb bones, and at least 120 osteoderms.

facts.statement: The generic name Yuxisaurus combines the type locality in Yuxi, Yunnan Province, China, with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, Yuxisaurus, combines a reference to the type locality in Yuxi, Yunnan Province, China, with the Greek "sauros", meaning "lizard."

facts.statement: Yuxisaurus lived during the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian-Toarcian) in the Fengjiahe Formation of southwestern China.
facts.quote: Yuxisaurus () is an extinct genus of early thyreophoran dinosaur from the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian-Toarcian) Fengjiahe Formation of southwestern China.

facts.statement: Yuxisaurus lived between 192.9 and 184.2 million years ago during the Pliensbachian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Pliensbachian to Pliensbachian (192.9 to 184.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Yao and colleagues identified Yuxisaurus as a basal member of the Thyreophora in their 2022 description.
facts.quote: In their 2022 description of Yuxisaurus, Yao and colleagues identified it as a basal member of the Thyreophora.

facts.statement: An implied weights analysis recovered Yuxisaurus as the earliest-diverging member of the Parankylosauria, though this result has poor statistical support.
facts.quote: Their implied weights analysis notably recovered Yuxisaurus as the earliest-diverging member of the Parankylosauria, a result that has poor statistical support but is based on at least two shared anatomical characters.

facts.statement: Analyses placed Parankylosauria outside Ankylosauria, recovering it as the sister taxon to Eurypoda or in an unresolved polytomy with those clades and Yuxisaurus.
facts.quote: Both analyses recovered Parankylosauria outside of its traditional placement within Ankylosauria. Instead, it was placed as the sister taxon to Eurypoda (ankylosaurs + stegosaurs) or in an unresolved polytomy with these clades and Yuxisaurus.

facts.statement: Yuxisaurus belongs to the parent group Thyreophoroidea.
Yuxisaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
